where: Section 1, definition of the Eulerian field
problem: The phrase 'components u, v and w, in m/s, along the axes x, y and z, in metres' is garbled: it makes the axes themselves seem to be measured in metres, and the student cannot tell which symbol carries which unit.
fix: Write: 'velocity components u, v, w in m/s along the x, y, z axes, where x, y, z are coordinates in metres'.

problem: 'Solving this first-order differential equation gives a family of curves with one constant' is true only for the two-dimensional form. In three dimensions dx/u = dy/v = dz/w gives two independent first-order equations, so a streamline is fixed by two constants (the intersection of two surfaces).
fix: State the one-constant family for the 2D case dy/dx = v/u, and note that in 3D two conditions (two constants) are needed to single out one streamline.

problem: The statement that the discharge through every section of a stream tube is the same is true for steady incompressible flow; in unsteady flow the volume between sections changes, and in compressible flow it is the mass flow ρAV that stays constant, not the volume discharge.
fix: Add the qualifier: in steady, incompressible flow the discharge Q = AV is the same through every section of a stream tube (more generally ρAV is constant).

problem: The example says the smoke rises 'in still room air', but Quiz Q7 explains the same smoke by saying the room air has draughts and is unsteady. A student meets two different settings for the same example, and in truly still air the rising smoke is a buoyant plume rather than a line of the room-air velocity field.
fix: Use one setting: 'Smoke rising from an incense stick in gently moving room air is a streakline; it marks the trail of particles that left the tip.' Keep Q7 consistent with this.

where: Section 2, first sentence of the streamline discussion
problem: 'A streamline freezes time and shows the whole field at that instant' overstates what one curve does: a single streamline shows the velocity direction only at the points lying on it, not the whole field.
fix: Say 'a streamline freezes time: it is drawn from the velocity field as it is at one instant'.

problem: 'the streakline from a chimney is what a monitoring station actually samples' is loosely worded: a station measures concentration at one fixed point as the plume passes, not the streakline itself.
fix: Say 'a monitoring station downwind sits in the plume that the chimney's streakline traces, and records how concentration at that fixed point changes with time'.
